What to plant in Ogun State

Quick answer: Ogun State is in Nigeria's South-West (Humid rainforest). The rainy season runs March – November (two peaks). Its best-known crops are cassava, water yam, sweet potato, tomato, hot pepper and okra. Plant rain-fed crops only after the rains have truly started.

RegionSouth-West
Rainy seasonMarch – November (two peaks)
VegetationHumid rainforest
Capital (weather point)Abeokuta

Questions farmers in Ogun ask

What crops grow best in Ogun State?

Cassava, Water yam, Sweet potato, Tomato, Hot pepper, Okra, Garden egg, Cucumber, Egusi melon, Amaranth (Efo tete), Celosia (Soko), Jute mallow (Ewedu), Waterleaf, Bitter leaf, Pineapple, Plantain, Banana, Pawpaw (Papaya), Sweet orange, Lime & Lemon, Guava, Cashew, Avocado, Coconut, African star apple, Cocoa, Oil palm, Rubber, Kola nut, Turmeric, Tannia (New cocoyam), Three-leaved yam (Bitter yam), Bitter kola, Velvet tamarind (Awin) and Lemongrass are among the best-known crops of Ogun State.

When does the rainy season start in Ogun State?

The rainy season in Ogun State usually runs March – November (two peaks). The rains have truly started when about 20 mm of rain falls within 3 days. Use our live check before you plant.

What can I plant in Ogun State in the dry season?

With irrigation or on fadama (wet valley) land: rice, white yam, tomato, cucumber, lettuce and sugarcane.

What should I plant in Ogun State at the start of the rains?

maize, cassava, white yam, water yam, cocoyam (taro), sweet potato, tomato and hot pepper are commonly planted when the rains begin.
